page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, aligned with compute-focused sizing. The CPU includes 16 MB of L3 cache, alongside standard hardware features such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration.

Hardware allocation excludes bundled local storage and dedicated GPUs, requiring attached remote block volumes for persistence. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations show middling single-threaded capabilities alongside modest multi-core throughput, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0 and a multi-core score of 2939.0. Extended instruction throughput and raw multi-threaded metrics, including stress-ng tests, rank in the lower percentiles relative to modern high-density compute options.

Cost efficiency is centered around standard baseline compute requirements where massive per-core throughput or local NVMe storage is unnecessary. While AES-accelerated encryption and single-threaded gzip compression perform adequately, database operations, static web serving throughput (4.07 GB/sec), and Redis operations (3.57 million ops/sec) reflect moderate bandwidth constraints. Consequently, the instance is suited for lightweight compute tasks, small backend web services, batch processing, and continuous integration workers that require dedicated vCPUs without extensive memory footprints.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. It offers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores alongside 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized resource ratio. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached storage and providing a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate moderate single-thread execution, highlighted by standard cryptographic and gzip compression speeds, but restrained multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth. Given its resource profile, ecs.c6a.xlarge is designed for lightweight compute-oriented tasks, modular microservices, CI/CD pipelines, and front-end application hosting that do not demand extensive memory capacity or high local I/O performance.
